Choosing a GLM engine: FSL, AFNI, or SPM

Source: vignettes/glm-engines.Rmd
glm-engines.Rmd

Suppose each participant completes two runs at each visit and you want the group mean response to a cue. All three engines can estimate it. Your choice determines how the two runs contribute to each person’s cue contrast and what information reaches the group model. The pipeline calls the time-series fit L1 and the group fit L3 in all three cases.

Choose this route when you need… How the runs enter the fit What reaches the group model
FSL for run-wise estimates, run-level predictors or precision weighting FEAT fits each run. A separate L2 model combines its COPEs (contrast estimates) using their VARCOPEs (estimated variances) in the default fixed-effects fit. FLAME can use the combined effect and its variance. A single-run analysis takes its inputs directly from L1.
AFNI for a shared task effect across runs, run-wise nuisance terms or explicit volume censoring One L1 model per participant and visit shares the cue coefficient across retained runs. Each run gets its own baseline and nuisance coefficients. An ordinary group GLM fits the contrast estimates by OLS. For repeated visits, 3dLMEr fits fixed and random effects to visit-specific estimates.
SPM for SPM condition and modulator designs or contrasts across run-specific coefficients By default each run is an SPM session in one first-level model per participant and visit. The default cue contrast averages the matching cue coefficients across runs. An SPM second-level analysis (pipeline L3) uses first-level contrast images. The wrapper generates a one-sample test or a multiple-regression design.

Run the same task with one engine

The quick start defines the three input tables and a clock_glm_spec.yaml with models named task, run_average, and group_mean. The example below uses that two-run design with a TR of 0.9 seconds. Set engine to one value and supply paths and nuisance settings for your study. If your cluster uses modules, configure the suite in parallel$compute_environment so the scheduled job can find the same installation.

library(fmri.pipeline)

engine <- "afni"  # "fsl", "afni", or "spm"
settings <- if (engine == "spm") {
  list(spm = list(spm_path = "/path/to/spm12", matlab_cmd = "matlab"))
} else {
  "default"
}

gpa <- setup_glm_pipeline(
  analysis_name = paste0("clock_", engine),
  scheduler = "slurm",
  trial_data = trial_df, run_data = run_df, subject_data = subject_df,
  tr = 0.9, n_expected_runs = 2L,
  glm_software = engine, glm_settings = settings,
  l1_models = NULL, l2_models = NULL, l3_models = NULL
)

spec <- "clock_glm_spec.yaml"
gpa <- build_l1_models(gpa, from_spec_file = spec)
if (engine == "fsl") {
  gpa <- build_l2_models(gpa, from_spec_file = spec)
}
gpa <- build_l3_models(gpa, from_spec_file = spec)

run_glm_pipeline(
  gpa, l1_model_names = "task",
  l2_model_names = if (engine == "fsl") "run_average" else "none",
  l3_model_names = "group_mean"
)

Here group_mean uses l3_input_mode: per_session, so each visit gets its own group analysis. The SPM and AFNI routes take their group inputs directly from L1. When building the SPM group model without an L2 specification, the builder can warn that L2/L3 compatibility has not been checked. This example needs no projected run-level predictors.

Coming from FSL

A pipeline signal supplies a task EV, and an L1 model selects signals and contrasts. The default use_preconvolve = TRUE passes sampled regressors to FEAT. Set it to FALSE at setup to have FEAT convolve onset/duration/value files. Check the EVs and contrasts in the generated .fsf and the fitted design.mat and design.con under feat_l1/. A completed run has a familiar .feat/stats/ directory with cope1.nii.gz and varcope1.nii.gz for the first contrast. FSL FEAT guide

If the second run was performed under a different condition, put that run-level predictor in run_data and include it in the L2 formula. Use l2_scope: id_session to keep one estimate per visit. Look in feat_l2/ and feat_l3/ for the higher-level .gfeat results. Choosing AFNI for L3 sends the FSL contrast estimates forward without their VARCOPE weights. For automatic pTFCE correction after L3 estimation, use the FSL group route described in the FWE guide.

Coming from AFNI

Start with the preprocessed runs you would normally pass to the regression step. Supply images on a common grid with comparable intensity scaling. Define timing and amplitudes in trial_data and the L1 model. The wrapper writes convolved task columns as -stim_file inputs to 3dDeconvolve. It records run boundaries and builds run-specific polynomial baselines (polort = "A" by default). For volume censoring, point run_data$afni_censor_file to a binary file per run, with 1 to keep and 0 to censor. Spike regressors in the confounds model are a separate choice.

By default 3dDeconvolve builds the design and 3dREMLfit estimates the time series with temporal prewhitening. Set glm_settings = list(afni = list(estimation = "OLS")) to fit by ordinary least squares in 3dDeconvolve. Inspect run_afni_glm.sh and design.xmat.1D under afni_l1/. Use contrasts.tsv to find a named GLT’s coefficient and t-statistic images. The coefficient image feeds L3. Ordinary group fits live in afni_l3/ and mixed models in afni_3dlmer/. AFNI 3dREMLfit help

Coming from SPM

A session column in run_data identifies a study visit. With the defaults l1_session_mode = "separate" and concatenate_runs = FALSE, two visits with two runs each produce two SPM.mat files per participant, each with two SPM sessions. Conditions and parametric modulators are generated from pipeline events and signals. The generated condition batch enables SPM orthogonalization, so modulator order can change what a coefficient measures. Inspect the fitted columns in SPM.xX.name and contrast weights in SPM.xCon. Pipeline defaults include a 100-second high-pass cutoff and cvi = "AR(1)". SPM model specification manual

Set options inside glm_settings$spm. Two choices change different aspects of the first-level design:

  • concatenate_runs = TRUE puts runs in one SPM session, sharing task columns, and invokes spm_fmri_concatenate with the run lengths.
  • l1_session_mode = "pooled" places runs from multiple study visits in one participant model. Keep the default for a separate model at each visit.

To model a run-varying predictor, build its L2 specification before L1 setup and select it with l2_projection_model. SPM can project its varying terms and requested task interactions into the first-level analysis. A predictor constant within an SPM session is aliased with the session constant as a main-effect column. Check the generated design and contrasts for the run comparison you intend.

Find SPM.mat, beta images and spm_contrasts.tsv under spm_l1/. The group setup matches contrast names to fitted con_*.nii files. Leave producer_backend unset for native SPM L3. The submission interface accepts explicit producer overrides only for FSL and AFNI. Inspect the group design under spm_l3/. The wrapper implements the flexible_factorial setting through multiple regression for non-intercept designs, preserving the pipeline design matrix and contrasts.

Use FSL estimates in an AFNI group model

A vector such as glm_software = c("fsl", "afni") enables both engines. For a longitudinal analysis, set that vector at setup. Specify which engine handles each stage on the resulting object:

gpa$level_backends <- list(l1 = "fsl", l2 = "fsl", l3 = "afni")

Build the FSL L2 model with l2_scope: id_session. Add the following L3 model to the YAML specification, with a visit covariate named session_label in your input data:

l3_models:
  visit_effect:
    level: 3
    model_formula: ~ session_label
    l3_input_mode: 3dlmer
    random_effects: "(1 | Subj)"
    execution_backend: afni
    producer_backend: fsl
    contrasts:
      diagonal: true

Here producer_backend identifies the suite that supplies the contrast maps. execution_backend identifies the suite fitting the group model. For an AFNI-only mixed model, choose AFNI at setup, use producer_backend: afni and skip L2. AFNI group models support one FSL or AFNI producer per model. The native SPM route uses its own first-level contrasts. See the longitudinal examples for visit comparisons and the design guide for run-time overrides.

At submission, check the backend preflight report in the log for the execution engine and the level supplying each group contrast. When comparing fits, check the retained volumes, mask, task columns, contrast weights and scaling for one participant first. For the cue example, a shared AFNI coefficient, an SPM contrast across run-specific coefficients and a precision-weighted FSL estimate can differ even with identical event onsets.

The whole-brain walkthrough follows a named contrast through the FSL output inventory. For post-fit work, consult the FWE guide for model-based pTFCE on FSL maps or standalone AFNI cluster correction, and the beta extraction guide for FEAT contrast estimates and masks.
